questions.question: Which of the following Mauryan inscriptions is NOT located in present-day India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kandahar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kandahar** is the Mauryan inscription that is NOT located in present-day India.
 
• Kandahar is currently in modern-day Afghanistan.
 
• The other inscriptions mentioned (Kalsi, Maski, and Girnar) are all located within the geographical boundaries of present-day India.
 
• The Mauryan Empire, under rulers such as Ashoka, had inscriptions spread across a vast region, including parts of present-day India, Nepal, Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Mauryan Empire** was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE and became one of the largest empires in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Ashoka, one of the most famous Mauryan emperors, is known for his widespread inscriptions and promotion of Buddhism.
 
• The inscriptions of Ashoka, written in various scripts and languages, are key historical sources for understanding the Mauryan period.
 
• These inscriptions were often engraved on rocks and pillars and served to propagate the policies and edicts of Ashoka, including his advocacy for dharma (moral law) and non-violence.

questions.question: Which of the following countries borders India to the north-west?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Afghanistan and Pakistan** are the countries that border India to the north-west.
 
• Pakistan shares a long border with India along the states of Jammu & Kashmir, Punjab, Rajasthan, and Gujarat.
 
• Afghanistan shares a shorter border with India, located at the north-western tip of Jammu & Kashmir, known as the Wakhan Corridor.
 
• This region is strategically significant for India due to its geopolitical and security implications.
 
• The border with Pakistan has been a focal point of various historical and political tensions between the two nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India** is bordered by several countries including China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, and Myanmar.
 
• To the north, India shares a long border with China, spanning the states of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• To the east, India shares borders with Bangladesh and Myanmar.
 
• India's border with Nepal and Bhutan lies to the north and north-east of the country.
 
• Each of these borders has its unique geopolitical and cultural significance, influencing India's foreign policy and regional dynamics.

questions.question: Banking regulation Act was passed in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1949**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Banking Regulation Act** was passed in the year **1949**.
 
• This act provides a framework for the regulation and supervision of commercial banks in India.
 
• The act was enacted to ensure sound and healthy banking practices and to protect the interests of depositors.
 
• It empowers the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to regulate, control, and inspect the banks in India.
 
• Key provisions of the act include licensing of banks, regulation of shareholding and voting rights of shareholders, and the management and operations of banks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Banking Regulation Act was initially known as the Banking Companies Act, 1949, and was later changed to Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
 
• The act extends to the whole of India and applies to all banking companies.
 
• It has been amended several times to address the changing needs and challenges of the banking sector.
 
• One significant amendment was made in 1965, which brought cooperative banks under the purview of the act.
 
• The act also lays down the procedure for the amalgamation and winding up of banks.
 
• The RBI has the authority to issue directives, inspect banks, and take necessary actions to ensure the stability and efficiency of the banking system.

questions.question: Which of the parts of the Indian Constitution deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part IV**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** are enshrined in **Part IV** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These principles are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. They are considered fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• The Directive Principles include provisions for securing and protecting a social order, right to work, education, and public assistance in certain cases, provision for just and humane conditions of work, and more.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• **The Directive Principles are inspired by the Directive Principles of Social Policy** enumerated in the Irish Constitution.
 
• **They aim to establish a welfare state by securing a social order based on social, economic, and political justice.**

questions.question: In any tennis game, if both players win three points each in a game (i.e. score is 40-40), then it's called a __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**deuce**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In tennis, a score of 40-40 is referred to as a **deuce**.
 
• When the score reaches deuce, a player must win two consecutive points to win the game.
 
• The first point won after deuce is called "advantage." If the player with the advantage wins the next point, they win the game; if they lose it, the score returns to deuce.
 
• This rule ensures that a player must lead by two points to secure a game after reaching deuce.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term **"deuce"** is derived from the Old French word "deus" meaning two, indicating that two more points are needed to win the game from this score.
 
• Tennis scoring can trace its origins back to medieval France, and the unique terms and scoring system have been retained over centuries.
 
• Understanding the concept of deuce is fundamental for anyone learning the rules and structure of tennis matches.

questions.question: What is the time period of the Eleventh five-year plan in India?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **The Eleventh Five-Year Plan** was implemented in India from **2007 to 2012**.
 
• This plan aimed at achieving faster and more inclusive growth.
 
• The focus areas included poverty reduction, education, health, infrastructure, and environmental sustainability.
 
• It was the penultimate plan under the Planning Commission, which was later replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans** in India were centralized and integrated national economic programs.
 
• The concept was borrowed from the Soviet Union, and the first plan was launched in 1951.
 
• These plans aimed at utilizing the country's resources efficiently to achieve set economic goals.
 
• The **Planning Commission** was responsible for the formulation and implementation of these plans until it was dissolved in 2014.
 
• The **Twelfth Five-Year Plan** (2012-2017) was the last one before the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog.

questions.question: In 1866, John Newlands, an English scientist, arranged the then known elements in the order of __________. It is known as 'Newlands' Law of Octaves'.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**increasing atomic masses**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1866, John Newlands, an English scientist, arranged the then known elements in the order of **increasing atomic masses**.
 
• This arrangement is known as **Newlands' Law of Octaves**.
 
• According to this law, every eighth element had properties similar to that of the first, much like the octaves in music.
 
• Newlands' Law of Octaves was one of the earliest attempts to classify elements based on their properties and atomic masses.
 
• This law was applicable only up to calcium, as beyond calcium, the properties of elements did not match the pattern.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• John Newlands' classification was an important step towards the development of the modern periodic table.
 
• Later, Dmitri Mendeleev and others improved upon Newlands' ideas, leading to the periodic table we use today.
 
• The periodic table is now based on the **increasing atomic number**, not atomic mass.
 
• Newlands' work demonstrated the periodicity of elements' properties, which is a fundamental concept in chemistry.

questions.question: The Green Revolution started in the year 1965 and the __________ five year plan was between 1961-1966.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3rd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India started in the year **1965**.
 
• The **3rd Five-Year Plan** was between **1961-1966**.
 
• The Green Revolution aimed to increase agricultural production through the use of high-yield variety seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation.
 
• This revolution led to a significant increase in food grain production, especially in states like Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The success of the Green Revolution made India self-sufficient in food grains and transformed the country from a food-deficient to a food-surplus nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **First Five-Year Plan** was from 1951 to 1956, focusing on the agricultural sector.
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan** (1956-1961) emphasized industrialization.
 
• The **Third Five-Year Plan** (1961-1966) aimed at making India self-reliant and self-generating in food grains.
 
• The Green Revolution was a part of the third plan and continued into the subsequent plans.
 
• It involved the introduction of new agricultural technologies and practices to increase productivity and ensure food security.

questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre, took place in consequence to the protest against the _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rowlatt Act**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on 13th April 1919.
 
• It was a direct consequence of the widespread protests against the **Rowlatt Act**.
 
• The Rowlatt Act was passed by the British government in India in March 1919.
 
• This act allowed certain political cases to be tried without juries and permitted internment of suspects without trial.
 
• It led to widespread anger and protests among the Indian populace, which culminated in the tragic massacre.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre was carried out by troops under the command of General Dyer.
 
• It took place in Amritsar, Punjab, where a large crowd had gathered for a peaceful protest.
 
• General Dyer ordered his troops to fire into the crowd, resulting in hundreds of deaths and thousands of injuries.
 
• The massacre is considered a turning point in Indian history, galvanizing the Indian independence movement.
 
• It highlighted the brutal nature of British colonial rule and intensified the call for complete independence (Swaraj).
